gates.description: CPU Gate: interpreter identity challenge, structured per-tool reports, actual in-container uid, and a typed finalized artifact -- each read from evidence, not from an exit code. Exit 0 with nothing run is a FAIL.

Runs one device workload as root inside the container, on an explicitly named device, with the identity assertion executed in-payload. A SHARED card is normal (HANDOFF section 4): occupancy is read first (before torch_npu/aclInit) and a busy card is RECORDED (busyRecorded=true), not refused; timings are provisional. Only health/readability (npu-smi unreadable/failed), identity (device id/binding/in-payload assertion) and ffi errors yield 75 BLOCKED_ENV.

busyDevicePolicy.default: RECORD occupancy and PROCEED: a shared card is normal and busy is allowed (HANDOFF section 4). busyRecorded=true; timings are provisional, numerics unaffected by contention.
busyDevicePolicy.refusalSet: ONLY health/readability (npu-smi unreadable or failed -> occupancy UNKNOWN), identity (device id, device not bound, in-payload assertion), and ffi errors yield 75 BLOCKED_ENV. Occupancy itself is NEVER a refusal reason.
busyDevicePolicy.ordering: Occupancy is still read in gate_device BEFORE torch_npu is imported, so a health problem is reported before any device node is opened. tests/device_policy.py enforces: occupancy precedes the probe, and NO branch returns BLOCKED_ENV conditioned on occupied.
busyDevicePolicy.legacy: TF_ALLOW_BUSY_DEVICE=1 is accepted but no longer needed; a busy card is allowed by default.
busyDevicePolicy.superseded: The previous policy REFUSED a busy card by default (with TF_ALLOW_BUSY_DEVICE as an override). That contradicted HANDOFF section 4 (shared card multi-user is normal; busy only recorded, never refused) and is replaced.
